claimChallenged: That Parmana's refusals are evidence: being prevention first, a refusal that works executed nothing, so nothing was signed and no trace remained (RFC-0021, Motivation).

source.attribution: A public technical objection raised twice; the commenter is not named in RFC-0021.

investigationSteps.method: Code-level trace of a REJECT through ExecutionGate.enforce, Runtime.execute, the API errorHandler and BusinessTransactionRepository (RFC-0021, Motivation). The exact date is not recorded; this is the latest date the cited sources support.
investigationSteps.observation: A REJECT threw before any signing or record building, no handler logged or stored it, and the accepted transaction row was never updated, so even the G-24 binding refusal left no durable evidence.

finding.statement: Every refusal is a durable, third-party-verifiable record would have been a false claim when the objection was raised.

outcome.description: Refusal Records: every policy REJECT reachable through RuntimeEngine.execute produces a signed, durable record, verifiable without the server or database (docs/CLAIMS.md 3.11); production audit-sink events are signed at write time.

disclosure.location: docs/rfcs/RFC-0021-Refusal-Record.md and docs/CLAIMS.md 3.11, in this public repository
